## The question

Richer countries generally live longer—but does a given level of income buy the same longevity everywhere, and has that relationship changed since 1990? A static scatterplot can show one year. It cannot conveniently reveal each country's identity, its path through time, or the regional patterns hidden underneath the global relationship.

I combine three World Bank indicators: GDP per capita at purchasing-power parity in constant 2021 international dollars, life expectancy at birth, and population. After removing regional aggregates and rows missing any of the three measures, the panel contains **6,597 country-year observations** and covers as many as 197 economies in 2023.

## Explore countries and years

The animated bubble chart makes four dimensions accessible: horizontal position is income, vertical position is life expectancy, bubble area represents population, and color identifies World Bank region. Use **Play** or drag the year slider; hover to identify a country; click a legend label to isolate a region; and double-click the legend to restore all regions.

<iframe class="plotly-frame" src="figures/figure1_income_health_responsive.html" title="Interactive animated scatterplot of GDP per capita and life expectancy by country from 1990 to 2023" loading="lazy"></iframe>

[Open the animation in a separate page](figures/figure1_income_health_responsive.html)

The cloud moves up and right, but it does not collapse onto one line. Across the countries with complete data, population-weighted life expectancy increased from **65.1 years in 1990 to 73.4 in 2023**, while population-weighted GDP per capita rose from approximately **$11,382 to $20,995**.

The cross-sectional gradient also flattened. An OLS regression of life expectancy on $\log_2(\text{GDP per capita})$ associates one income doubling with 4.47 additional life-years in 1990, compared with 3.65 years in 2023. This pattern is consistent with diminishing health returns to income, although the graph is descriptive and does not identify a causal effect.

The hover labels reveal why interactivity matters. In 2023, Jordan's life expectancy was about 6.6 years above the value predicted by the cross-country income relationship, while Nigeria's was about 15.3 years below it. These residuals direct attention toward health systems, conflict, inequality, disease burden, and measurement—not just average income.

## Switch between regional outcomes

The second figure aggregates countries using population weights. Choose **Life expectancy** or **GDP per capita**, hover over a line for exact values, and use the legend to compare selected regions.

<iframe class="plotly-frame short" src="figures/figure2_regional_trends_responsive.html" title="Interactive regional trends with buttons to switch between life expectancy and GDP per capita" loading="lazy"></iframe>

[Open the regional comparison in a separate page](figures/figure2_regional_trends_responsive.html)

South Asia recorded the largest life-expectancy gain, from 58.4 to 72.3 years. Sub-Saharan Africa also gained substantially—from 50.3 to 62.6 years—but remained far below every other region in 2023. Switching to GDP shows why a single global average is inadequate: East Asia and the Pacific experienced dramatic income growth, while Sub-Saharan Africa's population-weighted GDP per capita rose much more slowly.

## How the visualization is built

```python
fig = px.scatter(
    panel,
    x="gdp_per_capita",
    y="life_expectancy",
    animation_frame="year",
    animation_group="iso3",
    size="population",
    color="region",
    hover_name="country",
    log_x=True
)
fig.write_html("figures/figure1_income_health_responsive.html",
               include_plotlyjs=True)
```

`animation_group="iso3"` tells Plotly that the same country persists across frames. The logarithmic income axis makes proportional differences comparable, while hover labels preserve observation-level detail without covering the chart in text.

The takeaway is not simply that income and health are related. **Countries with similar income can achieve very different longevity, and those differences remain economically meaningful even after decades of global progress.** The animation, hover information, legend filtering, and metric selector let readers test that conclusion rather than merely accept a static summary.

**Data source:** [World Bank Open Data API](https://api.worldbank.org/), indicators `NY.GDP.PCAP.PP.KD`, `SP.DYN.LE00.IN`, and `SP.POP.TOTL`. The complete download, cleaning code, data, and interactive files are available in the [project repository](https://github.com/haozhuo22/blog-post-7-plotly-income-health).
